hints: Notice the total displacement from release to sea is downward: take upwards as positive so $s = -12 \text{ m}$ and $a = -9.81 \text{ m s}^{-2}$ with $t = 3.4 \text{ s}$.
Connect this to constant-acceleration motion with $s = ut + \frac{1}{2}at^2$, where the unknown is the initial velocity $u$.
Rearrange to $u = (s - \frac{1}{2}at^2)/t$, then substitute $s$, $a$ and $t$ and check the result is upward and near $13 \text{ m s}^{-1}$.
walkthrough: Choose upwards as positive. Then displacement to the sea is $s = -12 \text{ m}$, time is $t = 3.4 \text{ s}$ and acceleration is $a = -g = -9.81 \text{ m s}^{-2}$.
Use $s = ut + \frac{1}{2}at^2$ because $s$, $a$ and $t$ are known and $u$ is required for uniformly accelerated motion.
Calculate $\frac{1}{2}at^2 = 0.5 \times (-9.81) \times 11.56 = -56.7 \text{ m}$, so $u = \frac{-12 - (-56.7)}{3.4} = \frac{44.7}{3.4} \approx 13 \text{ m s}^{-1}$ upward.
